Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold).
- Key findings supporting diagnosis: Several days of cough with rhinorrhea, mild throat redness, no fever documented, no dyspnea or wheeze, normal breathing on exam, no focal chest findings.
- Differential diagnoses considered (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - ACE inhibitor-induced cough (Medium likelihood): Dry, hacking cough in a patient on lisinopril; could contribute or explain cough beyond infection alone. Timeline of lisinopril exposure not specified.
  - Acute bronchitis (Medium likelihood): Persistent cough after URI symptoms; may occur without lung exam abnormalities.
  - Influenza (Medium likelihood): Aches and chills present; duration fits; absence of fever lowers likelihood.
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan

- Immediate management: Reassurance and supportive care with over-the-counter options (Night Nurse / Day Nurse) recommended; paracetamol as needed for symptoms; no antibiotics or prescription required at this time.
- Follow-up and red flags: If symptoms worsen or new shortness of breath develops, or if symptoms persist beyond 3 weeks, contact clinician for possible examination (including chest exam).
- Medication adjustments: Continue current meds (metformin and lisinopril) unless new symptoms arise; no new prescriptions at present.
- Patient education: Use OTC nighttime and daytime cough/cold remedies as tolerated with current medications; monitor for progression or new symptoms.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) — High
  - Justification: Cough with rhinorrhea, mild throat redness, absence of dyspnea or focal lung findings, symptoms lasting several days.
- ACE inhibitor-induced cough — Moderate
  - Justification: Ongoing lisinopril use; dry, hacking cough could be drug-related; timeline not clarified.
- Acute bronchitis — Moderate
  - Justification: Persistent cough following URI symptoms; no objective chest findings, which can occur in viral bronchitis.
- Influenza — Moderate
  - Justification: Body aches and chills present; timing compatible; absence of fever lowers likelihood.
